blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 141 in June to 138 in September (−2.1%), and it took 25.6% of the city’s 215 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 220 in June to 210 in September (−4.5%), and it took 27.0% of the city’s 318 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Abbotsford West for detached houses in June (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July, August (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Fee-simple land

items.t: Urban lots: the detached stock across the urban part of the west side is fee-simple freehold under the Residential (RS) family of Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 — RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m², RS5 minimum interior lot 420 m², as stated in City rezoning reports. A bare lot in Clearbrook, Peardonville or Townline is a fee-simple parcel: no strata, no Form B, no strata fee; zoning, the OCP and any registered covenants or building scheme on title govern.

Rural and agricultural parcels (Mt. Lehman Road / YXX edge): acreage parcels with houses occur on the rural west and southwest edges. Servicing is the dividing line: lots outside the urban boundary in rural residential zones may NOT be connected to the Community Water System or Community Sanitary Sewer System and use wells and onsite sewage instead — "serviced" west-side land and "rural" west-side land are different products at different diligence.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the Agricultural Land Reserve covers rural parcels on the west and southwest edges, including land near Mt. Lehman Road and around YXX; the urban Clearbrook/Townline ground is non-ALR built subdivision land. The split is parcel-by-parcel, not street-by-street: whether a specific Mt. Lehman-side parcel is in the ALR is UNCONFIRMED until the ALC map and title are checked.

Airport overlay: airport height rules apply to land inside the Airport Zoning Regulation area around YXX, and floodplain boundaries are a schedule to the Zoning Bylaw (Schedule E – Floodplain Boundaries); Fishtrap Creek runs through the Ellwood / Fishtrap Creek Park area with streamside rules at development. Property-level status for any single lot must be checked in the City's WebMap.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Abbotsford West

items.t: Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs, at two scales: Urban: RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m², RS5 420 m². Rural: A1 minimum subdivision lot area 8.0 ha, A2 16.0 ha — the single most important number set for a west-side land buyer, because it decides whether a rural parcel can ever be split.

OCP: Abbotsforward 2050 is CURRENT: Abbotsford's current Official Community Plan is Abbotsforward 2050, adopted December 2025. The OCP's transit structure (Secondary Transit Corridors connecting Highstreet and the hospital to the Primary Transit Corridor on South Fraser Way between Clearbrook and McCallum Road) is the plan context for the Highstreet node's land values.

SSMUH / added units on a lot: Small Scale Multi-Unit Housing rules are in Zoning Bylaw s.140, and s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings, with City-report criteria including minimum lot size 400 m², minimum frontage 12.0 m, not on a cul-de-sac bulb and location on a Collector or Local road. Abbotsford's suite cap is under 50% of the principal dwelling, and a coach/garden suite is capped at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m² — Abbotsford's rules ONLY (standing corrections, commissioning brief, Nov 1, 2026). SSMUH does not override the A1/A2 minimums or the ALR on the rural edge.

ALR rules, on the west/southwest edge: subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval, stated as the ALC states it, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; Strata Property Act s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1)) — which is why no bare-land strata can be created out of ALR ground here. ALC residence caps: principal residence 500 m² or less; suite only within the principal residence; additional residence 90 m² (parcels of 40 ha or less) / 186 m² (over 40 ha). The City's A1 zone mirrors the added-dwelling route: one Accessory Farm Dwelling Unit per lot in accordance with the ALR Use Regulation, B.C. Reg. 30/2019, or as approved by the ALC, on a lot of at least 0.4 ha, at the same 90 m² / 186 m² caps.

Bare-land strata block (applies to every Downes Road Estates lot): a bare-land strata lot is strata tenure — Form B diligence (the lot's strata fee, amounts owed, approved levies, CRF balance, parking/storage and insurance summary; the strata must provide the Form B within 7 days of request, max $35 plus up to 25¢ per page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024 (30-year projections, at least three CRF funding models, non-deferrable by vote); minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (a directory "rentals allowed" line for Downes is in any event not a restriction); only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with legacy-resident, caregiver and the May 1, 2023 spouse/partner and defined-children exemptions) — which is why the "45+" marketing line noted in cannot stand as a bylaw and the registered bylaws govern.
Well and septic diligence (rural edge): A rural lot's price that assumes city services is mispriced ground.

First-home programs — the land boundary, stated precisely: the First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent MARCH 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122) applies to new HOUSING, not bare land itself — 100% of GST to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5 million, agreements on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031. A Downes Road Estates resale or a rural parcel attracts no such rebate; the question arises only on a qualifying new home. The GST New Housing Rebate (36%, maximum $6,300, $350,000–$450,000 phase-out) is likewise a housing rebate. Home Buyers' Plan $60,000 per buyer; First Home Savings Account $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year.
Market context, labelled as community-level only: SnapStats has NO land category — these are housing figures describing the market around the land, never land prices.

blocks.text: Good to know about Abbotsford West

items.t: The west side's one bare-land strata is filed "west" only because the MLS says so.

Downes Road Estates' own numbers conflict in the wild. Building directory: 51 units, built 1997. None of these is safe to quote singly — the strata plan (LMS2380), the Form B and the registered bylaws are the documents that settle count, age and fee.
A Mt. Lehman Road address is not the Mt. Lehman community.
The plan citation on most west-side pages is stale. The 2050 plan's transit-corridor structure around Highstreet is the current frame for west-side land, not the 2016 plan.
The only land-form 55+-marketed stock in the sub-area is Downes Road Estates, and even its age position is UNCONFIRMED on the registered bylaws.

faq.q: Can a house have a secondary suite or added small-scale units?
faq.a: Zoning Bylaw s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings, and City reports state suite criteria including a minimum lot size of 400 m² and minimum frontage of 12.0 m; Small Scale Multi-Unit Housing rules are in Zoning Bylaw s.140 — the zone for the lot controls what is allowed.

faq.q: Where is the main shopping for Abbotsford West?
faq.a: Highstreet Shopping Centre at Mt. Lehman Road, beside Highway 1 and the Highstreet Transit Exchange, is the main centre on the west side, with daily retail also along South Fraser Way at Clearbrook Road.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Abbotsford West than in June?
faq.a: In Abbotsford West, listings of houses fell from 141 in June to 138 in September (−2.1%); condos and townhomes fell from 220 in June to 210 in September (−4.5%).

faq.q: How big is Abbotsford West compared with the rest of Abbotsford?
faq.a: In September 2026, Abbotsford West held 31.4% of the 440 houses listed in Abbotsford and 36.7% of the 572 condos and townhomes listed in Abbotsford.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Abbotsford West from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 55 houses and 86 condos and townhomes sold in Abbotsford West over those 4 months.

faq.q: What kinds of land can I buy in Abbotsford West?
faq.a: Three: a fee-simple lot in an urban subdivision (Clearbrook / Peardonville / Townline), a bare-land strata lot at Downes Road Estates (32250 Downes Road, LMS2380 — a strata lot that carries a detached rancher, with strata fees and a Form B), or a fee-simple rural/ALR parcel toward Mt. Lehman Road and YXX. No named bare-land subdivision or presale lot offering was verified.

faq.q: What is a bare-land strata lot, in plain terms?
faq.a: Strata tenure applied to land: you own a strata lot (here, a lot with a rancher on it), you own a share of the common property by unit entitlement, you pay a bare-land strata fee, and the strata's bylaws bind the lot. It is NOT fee-simple — "Freehold Strata" on the title means strata, and the diligence is a Form B, not just a title search.
Treat the age position as UNCONFIRMED until the registered bylaws attached to the Form B are read, and do not rely on either marketing line.

faq.q: Can I split a rural parcel on the Mt. Lehman side?
faq.a: Almost never at house-lot scale: A1 subdivision minimum is 8.0 ha and A2 is 16.0 ha, and if the parcel is in the ALR, subdivision also requires ALC approval. Price a west-side acreage as one parcel unless the zone math and the ALR map both say otherwise.

Outside the urban boundary, no city connection is available in rural residential zones — those lots use wells and onsite sewage. Check the GWELLS well record and the Fraser Health sewerage filing before offering, and confirm which side of the urban boundary the parcel sits on; that line changes both servicing and price.

faq.q: Where does acreage actually trade in Abbotsford West?
faq.a: On the rural west and southwest edges — fee-simple rural and agricultural parcels toward Mt. Lehman Road and the airport lands, on well and onsite sewage where outside the urban boundary. The urban Clearbrook / Peardonville / Townline ground is house-lot ground, not acreage ground.

faq.q: How small a lot can I create in Abbotsford West?
faq.a: On the agricultural zones the City's parcel-size work records subdivision minimums of 8.0 ha (A1) and 16.0 ha (A2). In the urban zones, City rezoning reports applying the bylaw state RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m² and RS5 minimum interior lot 420 m² — confirm the specific zone's minimum with the City for the parcel.

faq.q: Which schools serve an address in Abbotsford West?
faq.a: Catchment is set by address in the SD34 School Locator. Recorded runs for three west-side addresses show the area splits: 3614 Clearbrook Road → Clearbrook Elementary → Colleen and Gordie Howe Middle → W.J. Mouat Secondary; 2990 Oriole Crescent → John MacLure Community School → Colleen and Gordie Howe Middle → W.J. Mouat Secondary; 3433 Firhill Drive → Blue Jay Elementary → Eugene Reimer Middle → Rick Hansen Secondary. Run any specific address before relying on a school.

faq.q: Is Carriage Lane a verified 55+ complex?
faq.a: Do not quote it as verified 55+ on the strength of the townhome count, and do not strike the townhome count on the strength of the age uncertainty.

faq.q: In Paradise Park, do I own the land?
faq.a: No. You own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act.

faq.q: Is Downes Road Estates the same tenure as Paradise Park?
faq.a: No — opposite forms. Downes Road Estates is bare-land strata: you own the strata lot (Form B, fees and bylaws apply). Paradise Park is pad rental: you own only the home. Do not compare their monthly costs or resale rules as if they were the same tenure.
A park's age rule lives in its park rules and tenancy documents, not in a strata bylaw; get the park's current rule in writing.
